<h1 id="bungienet-api">Bungie.Net API v2.21.9</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

These endpoints constitute the functionality exposed by Bungie.net, both for more traditional website functionality and for connectivity to Bungie video games and their related functionality.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://www.bungie.net/Platform">https://www.bungie.net/Platform</a> - The endpoint for accessing the Bungie.net API. You probably guessed that already.

<a href="https://www.bungie.net/en/View/Bungie/terms">Terms of service</a>
Email: <a href="mailto:support@bungie.com">Bungie.net API Support</a> 
Web: <a href="https://github.com/Bungie-net/api">Bungie.net API Support</a> 
License: <a href="https://github.com/Bungie-net/api/blob/master/LICENSE">BSD License 2.0</a>

<a href="https://github.com/Bungie-net/api/wiki/OAuth-Documentation">Our Wiki page about OAuth through Bungie.net.</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (apiKey)
    - Parameter Name: **X-API-Key**, in: header. Every request requires an API key.  To get an API key, register a new application at https://www.bungie.net/en/Application.

- oAuth2 authentication. For requests that require Authentication, you will need to have your users authenticate via our OAuth mechanisms.  See https://github.com/Bungie-net/api/wiki/OAuth-Documentation for more details.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://www.bungie.net/en/OAuth/Authorize](https://www.bungie.net/en/OAuth/Authorize)
    - Token URL = [https://www.bungie.net/Platform/App/OAuth/token/](https://www.bungie.net/Platform/App/OAuth/token/)
    - Refresh URL = [https://www.bungie.net/Platform/App/OAuth/token/](https://www.bungie.net/Platform/App/OAuth/token/)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|ReadBasicUserProfile|Read basic user profile information such as the user's handle, avatar icon, etc.|
|ReadGroups|Read Group/Clan Forums, Wall, and Members for groups and clans that the <br>user has joined.|
|WriteGroups|Write Group/Clan Forums, Wall, and Members for groups and clans that the <br>user has joined.|
|AdminGroups|Administer Group/Clan Forums, Wall, and Members for groups and clans that the <br>user is a founder or an administrator.|
|BnetWrite|Create new groups, clans, and forum posts, along with other actions that are reserved for Bungie.net<br>elevated scope: not meant to be used by third party applications.|
|MoveEquipDestinyItems|Move or equip Destiny items|
|ReadDestinyInventoryAndVault|Read Destiny 1 Inventory and Vault contents.<br>For Destiny 2, this scope is needed to read anything regarded as private. This is the only scope a<br>Destiny 2 app needs for read operations against Destiny 2 data such as inventory, vault, currency,<br>vendors, milestones, progression, etc.|
|ReadUserData|Read user data such as who they are web notifications, <br>clan/group memberships, recent activity, muted users.|
|EditUserData|Edit user data such as preferred language, status, motto, avatar selection and theme.|
|ReadDestinyVendorsAndAdvisors|Access vendor and advisor data specific to a user. OBSOLETE. This scope is only used on the Destiny 1 API.|
|ReadAndApplyTokens|Read offer history and claim and apply tokens for the user.|
|AdvancedWriteActions|Can perform actions that will result in a prompt to the user via the Destiny app.|
|PartnerOfferGrant|Can use the partner offer api to claim rewards defined for a partner|
|DestinyUnlockValueQuery|Allows an app to query sensitive information like unlock flags and values not available through normal methods.|
|UserPiiRead|Allows an app to query sensitive user PII, most notably email information.|

## App.GetApplicationApiUsage

<a id="opIdApp.GetApplicationApiUsage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/App/ApiUsage/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /App/ApiUsage/{applicationId}/`

Get API usage by application for time frame specified. You can go as far back as 30 days ago, and can ask for up to a 48 hour window of time in a single request. You must be authenticated with at least the ReadUserData permission to access this endpoint.

<h3 id="appgetapplicationapiusage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|applicationId|path|integer(int32)|true|ID of the application to get usage statistics.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|End time for query. Goes to now if not specified.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|Start time for query. Goes to 24 hours ago if not specified.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "Response": {
    "apiCalls": [
      {
        "datapoints": [
          {
            "time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
            "count": 0
          }
        ],
        "target": "string"
      }
    ],
    "throttledRequests": [
      {
        "datapoints": [
          {
            "time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
            "count": 0
          }
        ],
        "target": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "ErrorCode": 0,
  "ThrottleSeconds": 0,
  "ErrorStatus": "string",
  "Message": "string",
  "MessageData": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "DetailedErrorTrace": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="appgetapplicationapiusage-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Look at the Response property for more information about the nature of this response|Inline|

<h3 id="appgetapplicationapiusage-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Response|[Applications.ApiUsage](#schemaapplications.apiusage)|false|none|none|
|ErrorCode|integer(int32)|false|none|none|
|ThrottleSeconds|integer(int32)|false|none|none|
|ErrorStatus|string|false|none|none|
|Message|string|false|none|none|
|MessageData|object|false|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|string|false|none|none|
|DetailedErrorTrace|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: ReadUserData )
</aside>

## Forum.GetCoreTopicsPaged

<a id="opIdForum.GetCoreTopicsPaged"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Forum/GetCoreTopicsPaged/0/0/0/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Forum/GetCoreTopicsPaged/{page}/{sort}/{quickDate}/{categoryFilter}/`

Gets a listing of all topics marked as part of the core group.

<h3 id="forumgetcoretopicspaged-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|categoryFilter|path|integer(int32)|true|The category filter.|
|locales|query|string|false|Comma seperated list of locales posts must match to return in the result list. Default 'en'|
|page|path|integer(int32)|true|Zero base page|
|quickDate|path|integer(int32)|true|The date filter.|
|sort|path|integer(byte)|true|The sort mode.|

## Forum.GetPostsThreadedPaged

<a id="opIdForum.GetPostsThreadedPaged"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Forum/GetPostsThreadedPaged/0/0/0/0/true/true/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Forum/GetPostsThreadedPaged/{parentPostId}/{page}/{pageSize}/{replySize}/{getParentPost}/{rootThreadMode}/{sortMode}/`

Returns a thread of posts at the given parent, optionally returning replies to those posts as well as the original parent.

<h3 id="forumgetpoststhreadedpaged-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|getParentPost|path|boolean|true|none|
|page|path|integer(int32)|true|none|
|pageSize|path|integer(int32)|true|none|
|parentPostId|path|integer(int64)|true|none|
|replySize|path|integer(int32)|true|none|
|rootThreadMode|path|boolean|true|none|
|showbanned|query|string|false|If this value is not null or empty, banned posts are requested to be returned|
|sortMode|path|integer(int32)|true|none|

</aside>

## Forum.GetPostsThreadedPagedFromChild

<a id="opIdForum.GetPostsThreadedPagedFromChild"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Forum/GetPostsThreadedPagedFromChild/0/0/0/0/true/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Forum/GetPostsThreadedPagedFromChild/{childPostId}/{page}/{pageSize}/{replySize}/{rootThreadMode}/{sortMode}/`

Returns a thread of posts starting at the topicId of the input childPostId, optionally returning replies to those posts as well as the original parent.

<h3 id="forumgetpoststhreadedpagedfromchild-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|childPostId|path|integer(int64)|true|none|
|page|path|integer(int32)|true|none|
|pageSize|path|integer(int32)|true|none|
|replySize|path|integer(int32)|true|none|
|rootThreadMode|path|boolean|true|none|
|showbanned|query|string|false|If this value is not null or empty, banned posts are requested to be returned|
|sortMode|path|integer(int32)|true|none|

## Forum.GetPostAndParent

<a id="opIdForum.GetPostAndParent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Forum/GetPostAndParent/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Forum/GetPostAndParent/{childPostId}/`

Returns the post specified and its immediate parent.

<h3 id="forumgetpostandparent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|childPostId|path|integer(int64)|true|none|
|showbanned|query|string|false|If this value is not null or empty, banned posts are requested to be returned|

## Forum.GetPostAndParentAwaitingApproval

<a id="opIdForum.GetPostAndParentAwaitingApproval"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Forum/GetPostAndParentAwaitingApproval/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Forum/GetPostAndParentAwaitingApproval/{childPostId}/`

Returns the post specified and its immediate parent of posts that are awaiting approval.

<h3 id="forumgetpostandparentawaitingapproval-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|childPostId|path|integer(int64)|true|none|
|showbanned|query|string|false|If this value is not null or empty, banned posts are requested to be returned|

## GroupV2.GetGroupByNameV2

<a id="opIdGroupV2.GetGroupByNameV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/GroupV2/NameV2/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "groupName": "string",
    "groupType": 0
  }'
```

`POST /GroupV2/NameV2/`

Get information about a specific group with the given name and type. The POST version.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "groupName": "string",
  "groupType": 0
}
```

<h3 id="groupv2getgroupbynamev2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GroupsV2.GroupNameSearchRequest](#schemagroupsv2.groupnamesearchrequest)|true|none|
|» groupName|body|string|false|none|
|» groupType|body|integer(int32)|false|none|

|» HostGuidedGamePermissionOverride|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|Minimum Member Level allowed to host guided games<br>Always Allowed: Founder, Acting Founder, Admin<br>Allowed Overrides: None, Member, Beginner<br>Default is Member for clans, None for groups, although this means nothing for groups.|
|» UpdateBannerPermissionOverride|body|boolean \| null|false|Minimum Member Level allowed to update banner<br>Always Allowed: Founder, Acting Founder<br>True means admins have this power, false means they don't<br>Default is false for clans, true for groups.|

## Tokens.ApplyMissingPartnerOffersWithoutClaim

<a id="opIdTokens.ApplyMissingPartnerOffersWithoutClaim"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Tokens/Partner/ApplyMissingOffers/0/0/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /Tokens/Partner/ApplyMissingOffers/{partnerApplicationId}/{targetBnetMembershipId}/`

Apply a partner offer to the targeted user. This endpoint does not claim a new offer, but any already claimed offers will be applied to the game if not already.

<h3 id="tokensapplymissingpartnerofferswithoutclaim-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|partnerApplicationId|path|integer(int32)|true|The partner application identifier.|
|targetBnetMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|The bungie.net user to apply missing offers to. If not self, elevated permissions are required.|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /Tokens/Rewards/GetRewardsForPlatformUser/{membershipId}/{membershipType}/`

Returns the bungie rewards for the targeted user when a platform membership Id and Type are used.

<h3 id="tokensgetbungierewardsforplatformuser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|membershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|users platform membershipId for requested user rewards. If not self, elevated permissions are required.|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|The target Destiny 2 membership type.|

## Destiny2.GetDestinyEntityDefinition

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetDestinyEntityDefinition"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/Manifest/string/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/Manifest/{entityType}/{hashIdentifier}/`

Returns the static definition of an entity of the given Type and hash identifier. Examine the API Documentation for the Type Names of entities that have their own definitions. Note that the return type will always *inherit from* DestinyDefinition, but the specific type returned will be the requested entity type if it can be found. Please don't use this as a chatty alternative to the Manifest database if you require large sets of data, but for simple and one-off accesses this should be handy.

<h3 id="destiny2getdestinyentitydefinition-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|entityType|path|string|true|The type of entity for whom you would like results. These correspond to the entity's definition contract name. For instance, if you are looking for items, this property should be 'DestinyInventoryItemDefinition'. PREVIEW: This endpoint is still in beta, and may experience rough edges. The schema is tentatively in final form, but there may be bugs that prevent desirable operation.|
|hashIdentifier|path|integer(uint32)|true|The hash identifier for the specific Entity you want returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "Response": {
    "hash": 0,
    "index": 0,
    "redacted": true
  },
  "ErrorCode": 0,
  "ThrottleSeconds": 0,
  "ErrorStatus": "string",
  "Message": "string",
  "MessageData": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "DetailedErrorTrace": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="destiny2getdestinyentitydefinition-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

## Destiny2.SearchDestinyPlayerByBungieName

<a id="opIdDestiny2.SearchDestinyPlayerByBungieName"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/SearchDestinyPlayerByBungieName/0/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
```

`POST /Destiny2/SearchDestinyPlayerByBungieName/{membershipType}/`

|body|body|[User.ExactSearchRequest](#schemauser.exactsearchrequest)|true|none|

## Destiny2.GetLinkedProfiles

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetLinkedProfiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Profile/0/LinkedProfiles/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Profile/{membershipId}/LinkedProfiles/`

Returns a summary information about all profiles linked to the requesting membership type/membership ID that have valid Destiny information. The passed-in Membership Type/Membership ID may be a Bungie.Net membership or a Destiny membership. It only returns the minimal amount of data to begin making more substantive requests, but will hopefully serve as a useful alternative to UserServices for people who just care about Destiny data. Note that it will only return linked accounts whose linkages you are allowed to view.

<h3 id="destiny2getlinkedprofiles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|getAllMemberships|query|boolean|false|(optional) if set to 'true', all memberships regardless of whether they're obscured by overrides will be returned. Normal privacy restrictions on account linking will still apply no matter what.|
|membershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the membership whose linked Destiny accounts you want returned. Make sure your membership ID matches its Membership Type: don't pass us a PSN membership ID and the XBox membership type, it's not going to work!|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|The type for the membership whose linked Destiny accounts you want returned.|

## Destiny2.GetCharacter

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetCharacter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Profile/0/Character/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Profile/{destinyMembershipId}/Character/{characterId}/`

Returns character information for the supplied character.

<h3 id="destiny2getcharacter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|characterId|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the character.|
|components|query|[integer(int32)]|false|A comma separated list of components to return (as strings or numeric values). See the DestinyComponentType enum for valid components to request. You must request at least one component to receive results.|
|destinyMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|Destiny membership ID.|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|A valid non-BungieNet membership type.|

## Destiny2.GetClanWeeklyRewardState

## Destiny2.GetItem

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Profile/0/Item/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Profile/{destinyMembershipId}/Item/{itemInstanceId}/`

Retrieve the details of an instanced Destiny Item. An instanced Destiny item is one with an ItemInstanceId. Non-instanced items, such as materials, have no useful instance-specific details and thus are not queryable here.

<h3 id="destiny2getitem-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|components|query|[integer(int32)]|false|A comma separated list of components to return (as strings or numeric values). See the DestinyComponentType enum for valid components to request. You must request at least one component to receive results.|
|destinyMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|The membership ID of the destiny profile.|
|itemInstanceId|path|integer(int64)|true|The Instance ID of the destiny item.|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|A valid non-BungieNet membership type.|

## Destiny2.GetVendors

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetVendors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Profile/0/Character/0/Vendors/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Profile/{destinyMembershipId}/Character/{characterId}/Vendors/`

Get currently available vendors from the list of vendors that can possibly have rotating inventory. Note that this does not include things like preview vendors and vendors-as-kiosks, neither of whom have rotating/dynamic inventories. Use their definitions as-is for those.

<h3 id="destiny2getvendors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|characterId|path|integer(int64)|true|The Destiny Character ID of the character for whom we're getting vendor info.|
|components|query|[integer(int32)]|false|A comma separated list of components to return (as strings or numeric values). See the DestinyComponentType enum for valid components to request. You must request at least one component to receive results.|
|destinyMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|Destiny membership ID of another user. You may be denied.|
|filter|query|integer(int32)|false|The filter of what vendors and items to return, if any.|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|A valid non-BungieNet membership type.|

## Destiny2.GetVendor

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetVendor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Profile/0/Character/0/Vendors/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Profile/{destinyMembershipId}/Character/{characterId}/Vendors/{vendorHash}/`

Get the details of a specific Vendor.

<h3 id="destiny2getvendor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|characterId|path|integer(int64)|true|The Destiny Character ID of the character for whom we're getting vendor info.|
|components|query|[integer(int32)]|false|A comma separated list of components to return (as strings or numeric values). See the DestinyComponentType enum for valid components to request. You must request at least one component to receive results.|
|destinyMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|Destiny membership ID of another user. You may be denied.|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|A valid non-BungieNet membership type.|
|vendorHash|path|integer(uint32)|true|The Hash identifier of the Vendor to be returned.|

## Destiny2.GetPublicVendors

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetPublicVendors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/Vendors/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/Vendors/`

Get items available from vendors where the vendors have items for sale that are common for everyone. If any portion of the Vendor's available inventory is character or account specific, we will be unable to return their data from this endpoint due to the way that available inventory is computed. As I am often guilty of saying: 'It's a long story...'

<h3 id="destiny2getpublicvendors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|components|query|[integer(int32)]|false|A comma separated list of components to return (as strings or numeric values). See the DestinyComponentType enum for valid components to request. You must request at least one component to receive results.|

## Destiny2.GetCollectibleNodeDetails

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetCollectibleNodeDetails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Profile/0/Character/0/Collectibles/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Profile/{destinyMembershipId}/Character/{characterId}/Collectibles/{collectiblePresentationNodeHash}/`

Given a Presentation Node that has Collectibles as direct descendants, this will return item details about those descendants in the context of the requesting character.

<h3 id="destiny2getcollectiblenodedetails-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|characterId|path|integer(int64)|true|The Destiny Character ID of the character for whom we're getting collectible detail info.|
|collectiblePresentationNodeHash|path|integer(uint32)|true|The hash identifier of the Presentation Node for whom we should return collectible details. Details will only be returned for collectibles that are direct descendants of this node.|
|components|query|[integer(int32)]|false|A comma separated list of components to return (as strings or numeric values). See the DestinyComponentType enum for valid components to request. You must request at least one component to receive results.|
|destinyMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|Destiny membership ID of another user. You may be denied.|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|A valid non-BungieNet membership type.|

## Destiny2.InsertSocketPlug

<a id="opIdDestiny2.InsertSocketPlug"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/Actions/Items/InsertSocketPlug/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "actionToken": "string",
    "itemInstanceId": 0,
    "plug": {
      "socketIndex": 0,
      "socketArrayType": 0,
      "plugItemHash": 0
    },
    "characterId": 0,
    "membershipType": 0
  }'
```

`POST /Destiny2/Actions/Items/InsertSocketPlug/`

Insert a plug into a socketed item. I know how it sounds, but I assure you it's much more G-rated than you might be guessing. We haven't decided yet whether this will be able to insert plugs that have side effects, but if we do it will require special scope permission for an application attempting to do so. You must have a valid Destiny Account, and either be in a social space, in orbit, or offline. Request must include proof of permission for 'InsertPlugs' from the account owner.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "actionToken": "string",
  "itemInstanceId": 0,
  "plug": {
    "socketIndex": 0,
    "socketArrayType": 0,
    "plugItemHash": 0
  },
  "characterId": 0,
  "membershipType": 0
}
```

<h3 id="destiny2insertsocketplug-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[Destiny.Requests.Actions.DestinyInsertPlugsActionRequest](#schemadestiny.requests.actions.destinyinsertplugsactionrequest)|true|none|
|» actionToken|body|string|false|Action token provided by the AwaGetActionToken API call.|
|» itemInstanceId|body|integer(int64)|false|The instance ID of the item having a plug inserted. Only instanced items can have sockets.|
|» plug|body|object|false|The plugs being inserted.|
|» » socketIndex|body|integer(int32)|false|The index into the socket array, which identifies the specific socket being operated on. We also need to know the socketArrayType in order to uniquely identify the socket.<br>Don't point to or try to insert a plug into an infusion socket. It won't work.|
|» » socketArrayType|body|integer(int32)|false|This property, combined with the socketIndex, tells us which socket we are referring to (since operations can be performed on both Intrinsic and "default" sockets, and they occupy different arrays in the Inventory Item Definition). I know, I know. Don't give me that look.|
|» » plugItemHash|body|integer(uint32)|false|Plugs are never instanced (except in infusion). So with the hash alone, we should be able to: 1) Infer whether the player actually needs to have the item, or if it's a reusable plug 2) Perform any operation needed to use the Plug, including removing the plug item and running reward sheets.|
|» characterId|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» membershipType|body|integer(int32)|false|none|

This does not require 'Advanced Write Action' authorization and is available to 3rd-party apps, but will only work on 'free and reversible' socket actions (Perks, Armor Mods, Shaders, Ornaments, etc.). You must have a valid Destiny Account, and the character must either be in a social space, in orbit, or offline.

## Destiny2.ReportOffensivePostGameCarnageReportPlayer

<a id="opIdDestiny2.ReportOffensivePostGameCarnageReportPlayer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/Stats/PostGameCarnageReport/0/Report/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reasonCategoryHashes": [
      0
    ],
    "reasonHashes": [
      0
    ],
    "offendingCharacterId": 0
  }'
```

`POST /Destiny2/Stats/PostGameCarnageReport/{activityId}/Report/`

Report a player that you met in an activity that was engaging in ToS-violating activities. Both you and the offending player must have played in the activityId passed in. Please use this judiciously and only when you have strong suspicions of violation, pretty please.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reasonCategoryHashes": [
    0
  ],
  "reasonHashes": [
    0
  ],
  "offendingCharacterId": 0
}
```

<h3 id="destiny2reportoffensivepostgamecarnagereportplayer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|activityId|path|integer(int64)|true|The ID of the activity where you ran into the brigand that you're reporting.|
|body|body|[Destiny.Reporting.Requests.DestinyReportOffensePgcrRequest](#schemadestiny.reporting.requests.destinyreportoffensepgcrrequest)|true|none|
|» reasonCategoryHashes|body|[integer(uint32)]|false|So you've decided to report someone instead of cursing them and their descendants. Well, okay then. This is the category or categorie(s) of infractions for which you are reporting the user. These are hash identifiers that map to DestinyReportReasonCategoryDefinition entries.|
|» reasonHashes|body|[integer(uint32)]|false|If applicable, provide a more specific reason(s) within the general category of problems provided by the reasonHash. This is also an identifier for a reason. All reasonHashes provided must be children of at least one the reasonCategoryHashes provided.|
|» offendingCharacterId|body|integer(int64)|false|Within the PGCR provided when calling the Reporting endpoint, this should be the character ID of the user that you thought was violating terms of use. They must exist in the PGCR provided.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "Response": 0,
  "ErrorCode": 0,
  "ThrottleSeconds": 0,
  "ErrorStatus": "string",
  "Message": "string",
  "MessageData": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "DetailedErrorTrace": "string"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Look at the Response property for more information about the nature of this response|Inline|

## Destiny2.GetClanLeaderboards

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetClanLeaderboards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/Stats/Leaderboards/Clans/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/Stats/Leaderboards/Clans/{groupId}/`

Gets leaderboards with the signed in user's friends and the supplied destinyMembershipId as the focus. PREVIEW: This endpoint is still in beta, and may experience rough edges. The schema is in final form, but there may be bugs that prevent desirable operation.

<h3 id="destiny2getclanleaderboards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|integer(int64)|true|Group ID of the clan whose leaderboards you wish to fetch.|
|maxtop|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of top players to return. Use a large number to get entire leaderboard.|
|modes|query|string|false|List of game modes for which to get leaderboards. See the documentation for DestinyActivityModeType for valid values, and pass in string representation, comma delimited.|
|statid|query|string|false|ID of stat to return rather than returning all Leaderboard stats.|

## Destiny2.GetClanAggregateStats

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetClanAggregateStats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/Stats/AggregateClanStats/{groupId}/`

Gets aggregated stats for a clan using the same categories as the clan leaderboards. PREVIEW: This endpoint is still in beta, and may experience rough edges. The schema is in final form, but there may be bugs that prevent desirable operation.

|groupId|path|integer(int64)|true|Group ID of the clan whose leaderboards you wish to fetch.|
|modes|query|string|false|List of game modes for which to get leaderboards. See the documentation for DestinyActivityModeType for valid values, and pass in string representation, comma delimited.|

## Destiny2.GetLeaderboards

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetLeaderboards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Account/0/Stats/Leaderboards/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Account/{destinyMembershipId}/Stats/Leaderboards/`

Gets leaderboards with the signed in user's friends and the supplied destinyMembershipId as the focus. PREVIEW: This endpoint has not yet been implemented. It is being returned for a preview of future functionality, and for public comment/suggestion/preparation.

|destinyMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|The Destiny membershipId of the user to retrieve.|

|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|A valid non-BungieNet membership type.|
|modes|query|string|false|List of game modes for which to get leaderboards. See the documentation for DestinyActivityModeType for valid values, and pass in string representation, comma delimited.|

## Destiny2.SearchDestinyEntities

<a id="opIdDestiny2.SearchDestinyEntities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/Armory/Search/{type}/{searchTerm}/`

Gets a page list of Destiny items.

<h3 id="destiny2searchdestinyentities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Page number to return, starting with 0.|
|searchTerm|path|string|true|The string to use when searching for Destiny entities.|
|type|path|string|true|The type of entity for whom you would like results. These correspond to the entity's definition contract name. For instance, if you are looking for items, this property should be 'DestinyInventoryItemDefinition'.|

## Destiny2.GetHistoricalStats

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetHistoricalStats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Account/0/Character/0/Stats/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Account/{destinyMembershipId}/Character/{characterId}/Stats/`

Gets historical stats for indicated character.

<h3 id="destiny2gethistoricalstats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|characterId|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the character to retrieve. You can omit this character ID or set it to 0 to get aggregate stats across all characters.|
|dayend|query|string(date-time)|false|Last day to return when daily stats are requested. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD. Currently, we cannot allow more than 31 days of daily data to be requested in a single request.|
|daystart|query|string(date-time)|false|First day to return when daily stats are requested. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD. Currently, we cannot allow more than 31 days of daily data to be requested in a single request.|
|destinyMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|The Destiny membershipId of the user to retrieve.|
|groups|query|[integer(int32)]|false|Group of stats to include, otherwise only general stats are returned. Comma separated list is allowed. Values: General, Weapons, Medals|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|A valid non-BungieNet membership type.|
|modes|query|[integer(int32)]|false|Game modes to return. See the documentation for DestinyActivityModeType for valid values, and pass in string representation, comma delimited.|
|periodType|query|integer(int32)|false|Indicates a specific period type to return. Optional. May be: Daily, AllTime, or Activity|

## Destiny2.GetActivityHistory

<a id="opIdDestiny2.GetActivityHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Destiny2/0/Account/0/Character/0/Stats/Activities/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Destiny2/{membershipType}/Account/{destinyMembershipId}/Character/{characterId}/Stats/Activities/`

Gets activity history stats for indicated character.

<h3 id="destiny2getactivityhistory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|characterId|path|integer(int64)|true|The id of the character to retrieve.|
|count|query|integer(int32)|false|Number of rows to return|
|destinyMembershipId|path|integer(int64)|true|The Destiny membershipId of the user to retrieve.|
|membershipType|path|integer(int32)|true|A valid non-BungieNet membership type.|
|mode|query|integer(int32)|false|A filter for the activity mode to be returned. None returns all activities. See the documentation for DestinyActivityModeType for valid values, and pass in string representation.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Page number to return, starting with 0.|

## Trending.GetTrendingCategories

<a id="opIdTrending.GetTrendingCategories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Trending/Categories/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Trending/Categories/`

Returns trending items for Bungie.net, collapsed into the first page of items per category. For pagination within a category, call GetTrendingCategory.

## Trending.GetTrendingCategory

<a id="opIdTrending.GetTrendingCategory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Trending/Categories/string/0/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Trending.GetTrendingEntryDetail

<a id="opIdTrending.GetTrendingEntryDetail"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Trending/Details/0/string/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Trending/Details/{trendingEntryType}/{identifier}/`

Returns the detailed results for a specific trending entry. Note that trending entries are uniquely identified by a combination of *both* the TrendingEntryType *and* the identifier: the identifier alone is not guaranteed to be globally unique.

<h3 id="trendinggettrendingentrydetail-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|identifier|path|string|true|The identifier for the entity to be returned.|
|trendingEntryType|path|integer(int32)|true|The type of entity to be returned.|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```


`GET /Fireteam/Clan/{groupId}/Available/{platform}/{activityType}/{dateRange}/{slotFilter}/{publicOnly}/{page}/`

|page|path|integer(int32)|true|Zero based page|

|langFilter|query|string|false|An optional language filter.|

## Social.GetPlatformFriendList

<a id="opIdSocial.GetPlatformFriendList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/Social/PlatformFriends/0/string/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /Social/PlatformFriends/{friendPlatform}/{page}/`

Gets the platform friend of the requested type, with additional information if they have Bungie accounts. Must have a recent login session with said platform.

## .GetGlobalAlerts

<a id="opId.GetGlobalAlerts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://www.bungie.net/Platform/GlobalAlerts/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /GlobalAlerts/`

Gets any active global alert for display in the forum banners, help pages, etc. Usually used for DOC alerts.

<h3 id="getglobalalerts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|includestreaming|query|boolean|false|Determines whether Streaming Alerts are included in results|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "Response": [
    {
      "AlertKey": "string",
      "AlertHtml": "string",
      "AlertTimestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "AlertLink": "string",
      "AlertLevel": 0,
      "AlertType": 0,
      "StreamInfo": {
        "ChannelName": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "ErrorCode": 0,
  "ThrottleSeconds": 0,
  "ErrorStatus": "string",
  "Message": "string",
  "MessageData": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "DetailedErrorTrace": "string"
}
```

This contract supplies basic information commonly used to display a minimal amount of information about a user. Take care to not add more properties here unless the property applies in all (or at least the majority) of the situations where UserInfoCard is used. Avoid adding game specific or platform specific details here. In cases where UserInfoCard is a subset of the data needed in a contract, use UserInfoCard as a property of other contracts.

### Properties

|useTotalResults|boolean|false|none|If useTotalResults is true, then totalResults represents an accurate count.<br>If False, it does not, and may be estimated/only the size of the current page.<br>Either way, you should probably always only trust hasMore.<br>This is a long-held historical throwback to when we used to do paging with known total results. Those queries toasted our database, and we were left to hastily alter our endpoints and create backward- compatible shims, of which useTotalResults is one.|

|polls|[[Forum.PollResponse](#schemaforum.pollresponse)]|false|none|none|

|results|[[Forum.PostResponse](#schemaforum.postresponse)]|false|none|none|
|totalResults|integer(int32)|false|none|none|
|hasMore|boolean|false|none|none|
|query|[Queries.PagedQuery](#schemaqueries.pagedquery)|false|none|none|
|replacementContinuationToken|string|false|none|none|
|useTotalResults|boolean|false|none|If useTotalResults is true, then totalResults represents an accurate count.<br>If False, it does not, and may be estimated/only the size of the current page.<br>Either way, you should probably always only trust hasMore.<br>This is a long-held historical throwback to when we used to do paging with known total results. Those queries toasted our database, and we were left to hastily alter our endpoints and create backward- compatible shims, of which useTotalResults is one.|

|currentUserMembershipsInactiveForDestiny|boolean|false|none|A convenience property that indicates if every membership you (the current user) have that is a part of this group are part of an account that is considered inactive - for example, overridden accounts in Cross Save.|
|currentUserMemberMap|object|false|none|This property will be populated if the authenticated user is a member of the group. Note that because of account linking, a user can sometimes be part of a clan more than once. As such, this returns the highest member type available.|
|currentUserPotentialMemberMap|object|false|none|This property will be populated if the authenticated user is an applicant or has an outstanding invitation to join. Note that because of account linking, a user can sometimes be part of a clan more than once.|


Information about a current character's status with a Progression. A progression is a value that can increase with activity and has levels. Think Character Level and Reputation Levels. Combine this "live" data with the related DestinyProgressionDefinition for a full picture of the Progression.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|progressionHash|integer(uint32)|false|none|The hash identifier of the Progression in question. Use it to look up the DestinyProgressionDefinition in static data.|
|dailyProgress|integer(int32)|false|none|The amount of progress earned today for this progression.|
|dailyLimit|integer(int32)|false|none|If this progression has a daily limit, this is that limit.|
|weeklyProgress|integer(int32)|false|none|The amount of progress earned toward this progression in the current week.|
|weeklyLimit|integer(int32)|false|none|If this progression has a weekly limit, this is that limit.|
|currentProgress|integer(int32)|false|none|This is the total amount of progress obtained overall for this progression (for instance, the total amount of Character Level experience earned)|
|level|integer(int32)|false|none|This is the level of the progression (for instance, the Character Level).|
|levelCap|integer(int32)|false|none|This is the maximum possible level you can achieve for this progression (for example, the maximum character level obtainable)|
|stepIndex|integer(int32)|false|none|Progressions define their levels in "steps". Since the last step may be repeatable, the user may be at a higher level than the actual Step achieved in the progression. Not necessarily useful, but potentially interesting for those cruising the API. Relate this to the "steps" property of the DestinyProgression to see which step the user is on, if you care about that. (Note that this is Content Version dependent since it refers to indexes.)|
|progressToNextLevel|integer(int32)|false|none|The amount of progression (i.e. "Experience") needed to reach the next level of this Progression. Jeez, progression is such an overloaded word.|
|nextLevelAt|integer(int32)|false|none|The total amount of progression (i.e. "Experience") needed in order to reach the next level.|
|currentResetCount|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|The number of resets of this progression you've executed this season, if applicable to this progression.|
|seasonResets|[[Destiny.DestinyProgressionResetEntry](#schemadestiny.destinyprogressionresetentry)]|false|none|Information about historical resets of this progression, if there is any data for it.|
|rewardItemStates|[integer(int32)]|false|none|Information about historical rewards for this progression, if there is any data for it.|
|rewardItemSocketOverrideStates|object|false|none|Information about items stats and states that have socket overrides, if there is any data for it.|

<h2 id="tocS_Destiny.Definitions.DestinyStatDefinition">Destiny.Definitions.DestinyStatDefinition</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadestiny.definitions.destinystatdefinition"></a>
<a id="schema_Destiny.Definitions.DestinyStatDefinition"></a>
<a id="tocSdestiny.definitions.destinystatdefinition"></a>
<a id="tocsdestiny.definitions.destinystatdefinition"></a>

```json
{
  "displayProperties": {
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "icon": "string",
    "iconHash": 0,
    "iconSequences": [
      {
        "frames": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "highResIcon": "string",
    "hasIcon": true
  },
  "aggregationType": 0,
  "hasComputedBlock": true,
  "statCategory": 0,
  "hash": 0,
  "index": 0,
  "redacted": true
}
```

This represents a stat that's applied to a character or an item (such as a weapon, piece of armor, or a vehicle).
An example of a stat might be Attack Power on a weapon.
Stats go through a complex set of transformations before they end up being shown to the user as a number or a progress bar, and those transformations are fundamentally intertwined with the concept of a "Stat Group" (DestinyStatGroupDefinition). Items have both Stats and a reference to a Stat Group, and it is the Stat Group that takes the raw stat information and gives it both rendering metadata (such as whether to show it as a number or a progress bar) and the final transformation data (interpolation tables to turn the raw investment stat into a display stat). Please see DestinyStatGroupDefinition for more information on that transformational process.
Stats are segregated from Stat Groups because different items and types of items can refer to the same stat, but have different "scales" for the stat while still having the same underlying value. For example, both a Shotgun and an Auto Rifle may have a "raw" impact stat of 50, but the Auto Rifle's Stat Group will scale that 50 down so that, when it is displayed, it is a smaller value relative to the shotgun. (this is a totally made up example, don't assume shotguns have naturally higher impact than auto rifles because of this)
A final caveat is that some stats, even after this "final" transformation, go through yet another set of transformations directly in the game as a result of dynamic, stateful scripts that get run. BNet has no access to these scripts, nor any way to know which scripts get executed. As a result, the stats for an item that you see in-game - particularly for stats that are often impacted by Perks, like Magazine Size - can change dramatically from what we return on Bungie.Net. This is a known issue with no fix coming down the pipeline. Take these stats with a grain of salt.
Stats actually go through four transformations, for those interested:
1) "Sandbox" stat, the "most raw" form. These are pretty much useless without transformations applied, and thus are not currently returned in the API. If you really want these, we can provide them. Maybe someone could do something cool with it?
2) "Investment" stat (the stat's value after DestinyStatDefinition's interpolation tables and aggregation logic is applied to the "Sandbox" stat value)
3) "Display" stat (the stat's base UI-visible value after DestinyStatGroupDefinition's interpolation tables are applied to the Investment Stat value. For most stats, this is what is displayed.)
4) Underlying in-game stat (the stat's actual value according to the game, after the game runs dynamic scripts based on the game and character's state. This is the final transformation that BNet does not have access to. For most stats, this is not actually displayed to the user, with the exception of Magazine Size which is then piped back to the UI for display in-game, but not to BNet.)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|displayProperties|[Destiny.Definitions.Common.DestinyDisplayPropertiesDefinition](#schemadestiny.definitions.common.destinydisplaypropertiesdefinition)|false|none|Many Destiny*Definition contracts - the "first order" entities of Destiny that have their own tables in the Manifest Database - also have displayable information. This is the base class for that display information.|
|aggregationType|integer(int32)|false|none|Stats can exist on a character or an item, and they may potentially be aggregated in different ways. The DestinyStatAggregationType enum value indicates the way that this stat is being aggregated.|
|hasComputedBlock|boolean|false|none|True if the stat is computed rather than being delivered as a raw value on items.<br>For instance, the Light stat in Destiny 1 was a computed stat.|
|statCategory|integer(int32)|false|none|The category of the stat, according to the game.|
|hash|integer(uint32)|false|none|The unique identifier for this entity. Guaranteed to be unique for the type of entity, but not globally.<br>When entities refer to each other in Destiny content, it is this hash that they are referring to.|
|index|integer(int32)|false|none|The index of the entity as it was found in the investment tables.|
|redacted|boolean|false|none|If this is true, then there is an entity with this identifier/type combination, but BNet is not yet allowed to show it. Sorry!|

When a Stat (DestinyStatDefinition) is aggregated, this is the rules used for determining the level and formula used for aggregation.
* CharacterAverage = apply a weighted average using the related DestinyStatGroupDefinition on the DestinyInventoryItemDefinition across the character's equipped items. See both of those definitions for details. * Character = don't aggregate: the stat should be located and used directly on the character. * Item = don't aggregate: the stat should be located and used directly on the item.

A "Progression" in Destiny is best explained by an example.
A Character's "Level" is a progression: it has Experience that can be earned, levels that can be gained, and is evaluated and displayed at various points in the game. A Character's "Faction Reputation" is also a progression for much the same reason.
Progression is used by a variety of systems, and the definition of a Progression will generally only be useful if combining with live data (such as a character's DestinyCharacterProgressionComponent.progressions property, which holds that character's live Progression states).
Fundamentally, a Progression measures your "Level" by evaluating the thresholds in its Steps (one step per level, except for the last step which can be repeated indefinitely for "Levels" that have no ceiling) against the total earned "progression points"/experience. (for simplicity purposes, we will henceforth refer to earned progression points as experience, though it need not be a mechanic that in any way resembles Experience in a traditional sense).
Earned experience is calculated in a variety of ways, determined by the Progression's scope. These go from looking up a stored value to performing exceedingly obtuse calculations. This is why we provide live data in DestinyCharacterProgressionComponent.progressions, so you don't have to worry about those.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|displayProperties|[Destiny.Definitions.DestinyProgressionDisplayPropertiesDefinition](#schemadestiny.definitions.destinyprogressiondisplaypropertiesdefinition)|false|none|none|
|scope|integer(int32)|false|none|The "Scope" of the progression indicates the source of the progression's live data.<br>See the DestinyProgressionScope enum for more info: but essentially, a Progression can either be backed by a stored value, or it can be a calculated derivative of other values.|
|repeatLastStep|boolean|false|none|If this is True, then the progression doesn't have a maximum level.|
|source|string|false|none|If there's a description of how to earn this progression in the local config, this will be that localized description.|
|steps|[[Destiny.Definitions.DestinyProgressionStepDefinition](#schemadestiny.definitions.destinyprogressionstepdefinition)]|false|none|Progressions are divided into Steps, which roughly equate to "Levels" in the traditional sense of a Progression. Notably, the last step can be repeated indefinitely if repeatLastStep is true, meaning that the calculation for your level is not as simple as comparing your current progress to the max progress of the steps. <br>These and more calculations are done for you if you grab live character progression data, such as in the DestinyCharacterProgressionComponent.|
|visible|boolean|false|none|If true, the Progression is something worth showing to users.<br>If false, BNet isn't going to show it. But that doesn't mean you can't. We're all friends here.|
|factionHash|integer(uint32) \| null|false|none|If the value exists, this is the hash identifier for the Faction that owns this Progression.<br>This is purely for convenience, if you're looking at a progression and want to know if and who it's related to in terms of Faction Reputation.|
|color|object|false|none|The #RGB string value for the color related to this progression, if there is one.|
|rankIcon|string|false|none|For progressions that have it, this is the rank icon we use in the Companion, displayed above the progressions' rank value.|
|rewardItems|[[Destiny.Definitions.DestinyProgressionRewardItemQuantity](#schemadestiny.definitions.destinyprogressionrewarditemquantity)]|false|none|none|
|hash|integer(uint32)|false|none|The unique identifier for this entity. Guaranteed to be unique for the type of entity, but not globally.<br>When entities refer to each other in Destiny content, it is this hash that they are referring to.|
|index|integer(int32)|false|none|The index of the entity as it was found in the investment tables.|
|redacted|boolean|false|none|If this is true, then there is an entity with this identifier/type combination, but BNet is not yet allowed to show it. Sorry!|

Used in a number of Destiny contracts to return data about an item stack and its quantity. Can optionally return an itemInstanceId if the item is instanced - in which case, the quantity returned will be 1. If it's not... uh, let me know okay? Thanks.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|itemHash|integer(uint32)|false|none|The hash identifier for the item in question. Use it to look up the item's DestinyInventoryItemDefinition.|
|itemInstanceId|integer(int64) \| null|false|none|If this quantity is referring to a specific instance of an item, this will have the item's instance ID. Normally, this will be null.|
|quantity|integer(int32)|false|none|The amount of the item needed/available depending on the context of where DestinyItemQuantity is being used.|
|hasConditionalVisibility|boolean|false|none|Indicates that this item quantity may be conditionally shown or hidden, based on various sources of state. For example: server flags, account state, or character progress.|

So much of what you see in Destiny is actually an Item used in a new and creative way. This is the definition for Items in Destiny, which started off as just entities that could exist in your Inventory but ended up being the backing data for so much more: quests, reward previews, slots, and subclasses.
In practice, you will want to associate this data with "live" item data from a Bungie.Net Platform call: these definitions describe the item in generic, non-instanced terms: but an actual instance of an item can vary widely from these generic definitions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|displayProperties|[Destiny.Definitions.Common.DestinyDisplayPropertiesDefinition](#schemadestiny.definitions.common.destinydisplaypropertiesdefinition)|false|none|Many Destiny*Definition contracts - the "first order" entities of Destiny that have their own tables in the Manifest Database - also have displayable information. This is the base class for that display information.|
|tooltipNotifications|[[Destiny.Definitions.DestinyItemTooltipNotification](#schemadestiny.definitions.destinyitemtooltipnotification)]|false|none|Tooltips that only come up conditionally for the item. Check the live data DestinyItemComponent.tooltipNotificationIndexes property for which of these should be shown at runtime.|
|collectibleHash|integer(uint32) \| null|false|none|If this item has a collectible related to it, this is the hash identifier of that collectible entry.|
|iconWatermark|string|false|none|If available, this is the original 'active' release watermark overlay for the icon. If the item has different versions, this can be overridden by the 'display version watermark icon' from the 'quality' block. Alternatively, if there is no watermark for the version, and the item version has a power cap below the current season power cap, this can be overridden by the iconWatermarkShelved property.|
|iconWatermarkShelved|string|false|none|If available, this is the 'shelved' release watermark overlay for the icon. If the item version has a power cap below the current season power cap, it can be treated as 'shelved', and should be shown with this 'shelved' watermark overlay.|
|iconWatermarkFeatured|string|false|none|This is the active watermark for the item if it is currently Featured in-game. Clients should use the isFeaturedItem boolean to decide whether or not to show this as opposed to iconWatermark.|
|secondaryIcon|string|false|none|A secondary icon associated with the item. Currently this is used in very context specific applications, such as Emblem Nameplates.|
|secondaryOverlay|string|false|none|Pulled from the secondary icon, this is the "secondary background" of the secondary icon. Confusing? Sure, that's why I call it "overlay" here: because as far as it's been used thus far, it has been for an optional overlay image. We'll see if that holds up, but at least for now it explains what this image is a bit better.|
|secondarySpecial|string|false|none|Pulled from the Secondary Icon, this is the "special" background for the item. For Emblems, this is the background image used on the Details view: but it need not be limited to that for other types of items.|
|backgroundColor|object|false|none|Sometimes, an item will have a background color. Most notably this occurs with Emblems, who use the Background Color for small character nameplates such as the "friends" view you see in-game. There are almost certainly other items that have background color as well, though I have not bothered to investigate what items have it nor what purposes they serve: use it as you will.|
|isFeaturedItem|boolean|false|none|Whether or not this item is currently featured in the game, giving it a special watermark|
|isHolofoil|boolean|false|none|Whether or not this item is holofoil, which has special icon treatment and in-game appearance.|
|isAdept|boolean|false|none|Whether or not this item is adept, which has increased stats and/or perks.|
|screenshot|string|false|none|If we were able to acquire an in-game screenshot for the item, the path to that screenshot will be returned here. Note that not all items have screenshots: particularly not any non-equippable items.|
|itemTypeDisplayName|string|false|none|The localized title/name of the item's type. This can be whatever the designers want, and has no guarantee of consistency between items.|
|flavorText|string|false|none|none|
|uiItemDisplayStyle|string|false|none|A string identifier that the game's UI uses to determine how the item should be rendered in inventory screens and the like. This could really be anything - at the moment, we don't have the time to really breakdown and maintain all the possible strings this could be, partly because new ones could be added ad hoc. But if you want to use it to dictate your own UI, or look for items with a certain display style, go for it!|
|itemTypeAndTierDisplayName|string|false|none|It became a common enough pattern in our UI to show Item Type and Tier combined into a single localized string that I'm just going to go ahead and start pre-creating these for items.|
|displaySource|string|false|none|In theory, it is a localized string telling you about how you can find the item. I really wish this was more consistent. Many times, it has nothing. Sometimes, it's instead a more narrative-forward description of the item. Which is cool, and I wish all properties had that data, but it should really be its own property.|
|tooltipStyle|string|false|none|An identifier that the game UI uses to determine what type of tooltip to show for the item. These have no corresponding definitions that BNet can link to: so it'll be up to you to interpret and display your UI differently according to these styles (or ignore it).|
|action|object|false|none|If the item can be "used", this block will be non-null, and will have data related to the action performed when using the item. (Guess what? 99% of the time, this action is "dismantle". Shocker)|
|crafting|object|false|none|Recipe items will have relevant crafting information available here.|
|inventory|object|false|none|If this item can exist in an inventory, this block will be non-null. In practice, every item that currently exists has one of these blocks. But note that it is not necessarily guaranteed.|
|setData|object|false|none|If this item is a quest, this block will be non-null. In practice, I wish I had called this the Quest block, but at the time it wasn't clear to me whether it would end up being used for purposes other than quests. It will contain data about the steps in the quest, and mechanics we can use for displaying and tracking the quest.|
|stats|object|false|none|If this item can have stats (such as a weapon, armor, or vehicle), this block will be non-null and populated with the stats found on the item.|
|emblemObjectiveHash|integer(uint32) \| null|false|none|If the item is an emblem that has a special Objective attached to it - for instance, if the emblem tracks PVP Kills, or what-have-you. This is a bit different from, for example, the Vanguard Kill Tracker mod, which pipes data into the "art channel". When I get some time, I would like to standardize these so you can get at the values they expose without having to care about what they're being used for and how they are wired up, but for now here's the raw data.|
|equippingBlock|object|false|none|If this item can be equipped, this block will be non-null and will be populated with the conditions under which it can be equipped.|
|translationBlock|object|false|none|If this item can be rendered, this block will be non-null and will be populated with rendering information.|
|preview|object|false|none|If this item can be Used or Acquired to gain other items (for instance, how Eververse Boxes can be consumed to get items from the box), this block will be non-null and will give summary information for the items that can be acquired.|
|quality|object|false|none|If this item can have a level or stats, this block will be non-null and will be populated with default quality (item level, "quality", and infusion) data. See the block for more details, there's often less upfront information in D2 so you'll want to be aware of how you use quality and item level on the definition level now.|
|value|object|false|none|The conceptual "Value" of an item, if any was defined. See the DestinyItemValueBlockDefinition for more details.|
|sourceData|object|false|none|If this item has a known source, this block will be non-null and populated with source information. Unfortunately, at this time we are not generating sources: that is some aggressively manual work which we didn't have time for, and I'm hoping to get back to at some point in the future.|
|objectives|object|false|none|If this item has Objectives (extra tasks that can be accomplished related to the item... most frequently when the item is a Quest Step and the Objectives need to be completed to move on to the next Quest Step), this block will be non-null and the objectives defined herein.|
|metrics|object|false|none|If this item has available metrics to be shown, this block will be non-null have the appropriate hashes defined.|
|plug|object|false|none|If this item *is* a Plug, this will be non-null and the info defined herein. See DestinyItemPlugDefinition for more information.|
|gearset|object|false|none|If this item has related items in a "Gear Set", this will be non-null and the relationships defined herein.|
|sack|object|false|none|If this item is a "reward sack" that can be opened to provide other items, this will be non-null and the properties of the sack contained herein.|
|sockets|object|false|none|If this item has any Sockets, this will be non-null and the individual sockets on the item will be defined herein.|
|summary|object|false|none|Summary data about the item.|
|talentGrid|object|false|none|If the item has a Talent Grid, this will be non-null and the properties of the grid defined herein. Note that, while many items still have talent grids, the only ones with meaningful Nodes still on them will be Subclass/"Build" items.|
|investmentStats|[[Destiny.Definitions.DestinyItemInvestmentStatDefinition](#schemadestiny.definitions.destinyiteminvestmentstatdefinition)]|false|none|If the item has stats, this block will be defined. It has the "raw" investment stats for the item. These investment stats don't take into account the ways that the items can spawn, nor do they take into account any Stat Group transformations. I have retained them for debugging purposes, but I do not know how useful people will find them.|
|perks|[[Destiny.Definitions.DestinyItemPerkEntryDefinition](#schemadestiny.definitions.destinyitemperkentrydefinition)]|false|none|If the item has any *intrinsic* Perks (Perks that it will provide regardless of Sockets, Talent Grid, and other transitory state), they will be defined here.|
|loreHash|integer(uint32) \| null|false|none|If the item has any related Lore (DestinyLoreDefinition), this will be the hash identifier you can use to look up the lore definition.|
|summaryItemHash|integer(uint32) \| null|false|none|There are times when the game will show you a "summary/vague" version of an item - such as a description of its type represented as a DestinyInventoryItemDefinition - rather than display the item itself.<br>This happens sometimes when summarizing possible rewards in a tooltip. This is the item displayed instead, if it exists.|
|animations|[[Destiny.Definitions.Animations.DestinyAnimationReference](#schemadestiny.definitions.animations.destinyanimationreference)]|false|none|If any animations were extracted from game content for this item, these will be the definitions of those animations.|
|allowActions|boolean|false|none|BNet may forbid the execution of actions on this item via the API. If that is occurring, allowActions will be set to false.|
|links|[[Links.HyperlinkReference](#schemalinks.hyperlinkreference)]|false|none|If we added any help or informational URLs about this item, these will be those links.|
|doesPostmasterPullHaveSideEffects|boolean|false|none|The boolean will indicate to us (and you!) whether something *could* happen when you transfer this item from the Postmaster that might be considered a "destructive" action.<br>It is not feasible currently to tell you (or ourelves!) in a consistent way whether this *will* actually cause a destructive action, so we are playing it safe: if it has the potential to do so, we will not allow it to be transferred from the Postmaster by default. You will need to check for this flag before transferring an item from the Postmaster, or else you'll end up receiving an error.|
|nonTransferrable|boolean|false|none|The intrinsic transferability of an item.<br>I hate that this boolean is negative - but there's a reason.<br>Just because an item is intrinsically transferrable doesn't mean that it can be transferred, and we don't want to imply that this is the only source of that transferability.|
|itemCategoryHashes|[integer(uint32)]|false|none|BNet attempts to make a more formal definition of item "Categories", as defined by DestinyItemCategoryDefinition. This is a list of all Categories that we were able to algorithmically determine that this item is a member of. (for instance, that it's a "Weapon", that it's an "Auto Rifle", etc...)<br>The algorithm for these is, unfortunately, volatile. If you believe you see a miscategorized item, please let us know on the Bungie API forums.|
|specialItemType|integer(int32)|false|none|In Destiny 1, we identified some items as having particular categories that we'd like to know about for various internal logic purposes. These are defined in SpecialItemType, and while these days the itemCategoryHashes are the preferred way of identifying types, we have retained this enum for its convenience.|
|itemType|integer(int32)|false|none|A value indicating the "base" the of the item. This enum is a useful but dramatic oversimplification of what it means for an item to have a "Type". Still, it's handy in many situations.<br>itemCategoryHashes are the preferred way of identifying types, we have retained this enum for its convenience.|
|itemSubType|integer(int32)|false|none|A value indicating the "sub-type" of the item. For instance, where an item might have an itemType value "Weapon", this will be something more specific like "Auto Rifle".<br>itemCategoryHashes are the preferred way of identifying types, we have retained this enum for its convenience.|
|classType|integer(int32)|false|none|We run a similarly weak-sauce algorithm to try and determine whether an item is restricted to a specific class. If we find it to be restricted in such a way, we set this classType property to match the class' enumeration value so that users can easily identify class restricted items.<br>If you see a mis-classed item, please inform the developers in the Bungie API forum.|
|breakerType|integer(int32)|false|none|Some weapons and plugs can have a "Breaker Type": a special ability that works sort of like damage type vulnerabilities. This is (almost?) always set on items by plugs.|
|breakerTypeHash|integer(uint32) \| null|false|none|Since we also have a breaker type definition, this is the hash for that breaker type for your convenience. Whether you use the enum or hash and look up the definition depends on what's cleanest for your code.|
|equippable|boolean|false|none|If true, then you will be allowed to equip the item if you pass its other requirements.<br>This being false means that you cannot equip the item under any circumstances.|
|damageTypeHashes|[integer(uint32)]|false|none|Theoretically, an item can have many possible damage types. In *practice*, this is not true, but just in case weapons start being made that have multiple (for instance, an item where a socket has reusable plugs for every possible damage type that you can choose from freely), this field will return all of the possible damage types that are available to the weapon by default.|
|damageTypes|[integer(int32)]|false|none|This is the list of all damage types that we know ahead of time the item can take on. Unfortunately, this does not preclude the possibility of something funky happening to give the item a damage type that cannot be predicted beforehand: for example, if some designer decides to create arbitrary non-reusable plugs that cause damage type to change.<br>This damage type prediction will only use the following to determine potential damage types:<br>- Intrinsic perks<br>- Talent Node perks<br>- Known, reusable plugs for sockets|
|defaultDamageType|integer(int32)|false|none|If the item has a damage type that could be considered to be default, it will be populated here.<br>For various upsetting reasons, it's surprisingly cumbersome to figure this out. I hope you're happy.|
|defaultDamageTypeHash|integer(uint32) \| null|false|none|Similar to defaultDamageType, but represented as the hash identifier for a DestinyDamageTypeDefinition.<br>I will likely regret leaving in the enumeration versions of these properties, but for now they're very convenient.|
|seasonHash|integer(uint32) \| null|false|none|If this item is related directly to a Season of Destiny, this is the hash identifier for that season.|
|isWrapper|boolean|false|none|If true, this is a dummy vendor-wrapped item template. Items purchased from Eververse will be "wrapped" by one of these items so that we can safely provide refund capabilities before the item is "unwrapped".|
|traitIds|[string]|false|none|Traits are metadata tags applied to this item. For example: armor slot, weapon type, foundry, faction, etc. These IDs come from the game and don't map to any content, but should still be useful.|
|traitHashes|[integer(uint32)]|false|none|These are the corresponding trait definition hashes for the entries in traitIds.|
|hash|integer(uint32)|false|none|The unique identifier for this entity. Guaranteed to be unique for the type of entity, but not globally.<br>When entities refer to each other in Destiny content, it is this hash that they are referring to.|
|index|integer(int32)|false|none|The index of the entity as it was found in the investment tables.|
|redacted|boolean|false|none|If this is true, then there is an entity with this identifier/type combination, but BNet is not yet allowed to show it. Sorry!|

<h2 id="tocS_Destiny.Definitions.DestinyItemActionBlockDefinition">Destiny.Definitions.DestinyItemActionBlockDefinition</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadestiny.definitions.destinyitemactionblockdefinition"></a>
<a id="schema_Destiny.Definitions.DestinyItemActionBlockDefinition"></a>
<a id="tocSdestiny.definitions.destinyitemactionblockdefinition"></a>
<a id="tocsdestiny.definitions.destinyitemactionblockdefinition"></a>

```json
{
  "verbName": "string",
  "verbDescription": "string",
  "isPositive": true,
  "overlayScreenName": "string",
  "overlayIcon": "string",
  "requiredCooldownSeconds": 0,
  "requiredItems": [
    {
      "count": 0,
      "itemHash": 0,
      "deleteOnAction": true
    }
  ],
  "progressionRewards": [
    {
      "progressionMappingHash": 0,
      "amount": 0,
      "applyThrottles": true
    }
  ],
  "actionTypeLabel": "string",
  "requiredLocation": "string",
  "requiredCooldownHash": 0,
  "deleteOnAction": true,
  "consumeEntireStack": true,
  "useOnAcquire": true
}
```

If an item can have an action performed on it (like "Dismantle"), it will be defined here if you care.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|verbName|string|false|none|Localized text for the verb of the action being performed.|
|verbDescription|string|false|none|Localized text describing the action being performed.|
|isPositive|boolean|false|none|The content has this property, however it's not entirely clear how it is used.|
|overlayScreenName|string|false|none|If the action has an overlay screen associated with it, this is the name of that screen. Unfortunately, we cannot return the screen's data itself.|
|overlayIcon|string|false|none|The icon associated with the overlay screen for the action, if any.|
|requiredCooldownSeconds|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of seconds to delay before allowing this action to be performed again.|
|requiredItems|[[Destiny.Definitions.DestinyItemActionRequiredItemDefinition](#schemadestiny.definitions.destinyitemactionrequireditemdefinition)]|false|none|If the action requires other items to exist or be destroyed, this is the list of those items and requirements.|
|progressionRewards|[[Destiny.Definitions.DestinyProgressionRewardDefinition](#schemadestiny.definitions.destinyprogressionrewarddefinition)]|false|none|If performing this action earns you Progression, this is the list of progressions and values granted for those progressions by performing this action.|
|actionTypeLabel|string|false|none|The internal identifier for the action.|
|requiredLocation|string|false|none|Theoretically, an item could have a localized string for a hint about the location in which the action should be performed. In practice, no items yet have this property.|
|requiredCooldownHash|integer(uint32)|false|none|The identifier hash for the Cooldown associated with this action. We have not pulled this data yet for you to have more data to use for cooldowns.|
|deleteOnAction|boolean|false|none|If true, the item is deleted when the action completes.|
|consumeEntireStack|boolean|false|none|If true, the entire stack is deleted when the action completes.|
|useOnAcquire|boolean|false|none|If true, this action will be performed as soon as you earn this item. Some rewards work this way, providing you a single item to pick up from a reward-granting vendor in-game and then immediately consuming itself to provide you multiple items.|
